results.description: Most expressive text-to-speech model from Inworld, with natural-language steering, real-time latency, and multilingual support across 100+ languages.

text.title: Text
text.description: The text to convert to speech. Maximum 2,000 characters. Supports natural-language steering with bracketed instructions placed before the text they apply to (e.g. `[say excitedly]`, `[whisper in a hushed style]`, `[say sadly with deliberate pauses in a low voice]`). Inline non-verbal tags are also supported (e.g. `[laugh]`, `[sigh]`, `[breathe]`, `[clear throat]`, `[cough]`, `[yawn]`). SSML break tags work for pauses (e.g. `<break time="1s" />`). Capitalize words for emphasis (e.g. `I told you NOT to do that`).

language.description: Language of the input text. Use 'auto' to let the model detect the language. Supported production languages: English (en), Chinese (zh), Japanese (ja), Korean (ko), Russian (ru), Italian (it), Spanish (es), Portuguese (pt), French (fr), German (de), Polish (pl), Dutch (nl), Hindi (hi), Hebrew (he), Arabic (ar).

voice_id.title: Voice Id
voice_id.description: The voice to use. Use a preset voice name (e.g. 'Ashley', 'Dennis', 'Alex', 'Darlene') or a custom cloned voice ID.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: Controls randomness when generating audio. Higher values produce more expressive results, lower values are more deterministic. Set to 0 to use the model default (1.1).

speaking_rate.title: Speaking Rate
speaking_rate.description: Speaking speed multiplier. Set to 0 for normal speed (1.0).

text_normalization.description: Controls whether numbers, dates, and abbreviations are expanded before synthesis. 'auto' lets the model decide, 'on' always normalizes, 'off' reads text as-is.

results.description: creates vector style thumbnails for blog posts.

mask.title: Mask
mask.description: Image mask for image inpainting mode. If provided, aspect_ratio, width, and height inputs are ignored.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Random seed. Set for reproducible generation

image.title: Image
image.description: Input image for image to image or inpainting mode. If provided, aspect_ratio, width, and height inputs are ignored.

model.description: Which model to run inference with. The dev model performs best with around 28 inference steps but the schnell model only needs 4 steps.

width.title: Width
width.description: Width of generated image. Only works if `aspect_ratio` is set to custom. Will be rounded to nearest multiple of 16. Incompatible with fast generation

height.title: Height
height.description: Height of generated image. Only works if `aspect_ratio` is set to custom. Will be rounded to nearest multiple of 16. Incompatible with fast generation

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Prompt for generated image. If you include the `trigger_word` used in the training process you are more likely to activate the trained object, style, or concept in the resulting image.

go_fast.title: Go Fast
go_fast.description: Run faster predictions with model optimized for speed (currently fp8 quantized); disable to run in original bf16

extra_lora.title: Extra Lora
extra_lora.description: Load LoRA weights. Supports Replicate models in the format <owner>/<username> or <owner>/<username>/<version>, HuggingFace URLs in the format huggingface.co/<owner>/<model-name>, CivitAI URLs in the format civitai.com/models/<id>[/<model-name>], or arbitrary .safetensors URLs from the Internet. For example, 'fofr/flux-pixar-cars'

lora_scale.title: Lora Scale
lora_scale.description: Determines how strongly the main LoRA should be applied. Sane results between 0 and 1 for base inference. For go_fast we apply a 1.5x multiplier to this value; we've generally seen good performance when scaling the base value by that amount. You may still need to experiment to find the best value for your particular lora.

input.prompt: Explain quantum computing in simple terms

default_example.output:
To understand quantum computing, you first have to understand how a **classical computer** (the phone or laptop you are using right now) works.

### 1. The Classical Way: Bits
Classical computers use **Bits**. A bit is like a light switch: it can be either **Off (0)** or **On (1)**. 

Everything you do on a computer—typing an email, watching a video, playing a game—is just billions of these 0s and 1s flipping on and off in different combinations. It’s very fast, but it can only do one thing at a time: it processes a sequence of steps.

### 2. The Quantum Way: Qubits
Quantum computers use **Qubits**. These are based on the laws of quantum physics, and they have two "superpowers" that make them different from regular bits:

#### Superpower #1: Superposition (The Spinning Coin)
